title: Sell Mineral Rights in Burlington, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Burlington, WY | Big Horn Co.
metaDescription: Burlington, WY sits in Big Horn County's irrigated farm belt near legacy oil fields. Get a courthouse-checked read on your mineral interest before selling.
heroLead: Burlington grew up as an irrigated farming community off the Bighorn River, and the mineral interests I find here usually trace to the same reclamation-era homestead patents that brought sugar beet farming to this part of the county.
intro: Big Horn County's early irrigation projects turned Burlington and the surrounding bottomland into productive farm ground in the early 1900s, and those original homestead patents came with full mineral rights attached. Over the following decades, as the Bighorn Basin's oil fields developed nearby, plenty of that mineral estate got severed off through lease bonuses, sales, or simple inheritance splits that separated it from the farm above.
If your family has farmed this ground for generations, there's a real chance a mineral interest is still sitting in the family name, disconnected from who's actually working the land today.

sections.heading: Farm ground over oil ground
paragraphs: Burlington itself sits a bit removed from the county's most active legacy fields like Elk Basin and Byron, so most interests here price as undeveloped or lightly-developed acreage rather than currently producing minerals. That said, courthouse records show real historical leasing activity across this area going back decades.
I check your specific section against known field boundaries and lease history before saying which category applies to your interest.

sections.heading: Sorting out farm-family fractions
paragraphs: It's common for Burlington-area mineral interests to have split among multiple heirs over several generations, sometimes without anyone keeping clean track of who holds what. I work from whatever documentation exists, a deed, a tax notice, a probate order, to establish your actual fractional share through the Big Horn County recorder.

Because so many of these interests trace to the same handful of original irrigation-district patents, I sometimes find that neighboring families hold interconnected fractions in the same or adjacent tracts, a detail worth knowing if you're weighing whether to sell alongside relatives or independently.

faqs.question: Does my irrigation water right affect my mineral rights?
faqs.answer: No, they're entirely separate legal interests. Selling minerals has no bearing on your water rights or farming operation.

faqs.question: Has anyone drilled near Burlington?
faqs.answer: There's historical activity in the broader area, but I'll check your specific section's lease and production record before answering for your tract.

faqs.question: What if I only inherited a small fraction?
faqs.answer: Small fractional interests still have real value. I'll quote yours based on your actual documented share.

faqs.question: Can you work with an old probate order instead of a deed?
faqs.answer: Yes, a probate order is often exactly what I need to confirm how an interest passed to you.
